output.title: When template reuse is worth measuring
output.body:
Template reuse is only useful to measure when it points to a real workflow decision.

If you run a small business, the question is not “can I count templates?” It is: which recurring workflow keeps producing the same document, email, or proposal, and do I actually need visibility into that pattern?

Start with one place only. Pick customer emails, proposals, or invoices for one month. List the templates you used, where they live, and whether you can tell which version is current. If that already feels messy, you have found a diagnostic worth paying attention to.

The next step is still manual: do a quick hand audit before you automate anything. Count distinct templates, note how often each one shows up, and check whether reuse is obvious or hidden across folders, inboxes, or SaaS tools. That tells you whether the problem is simple clutter or a workflow worth tracking.

Keep the human boundary clear. If the data suggests a template should be merged, retired, or left alone, the owner makes that call. Automation should surface the pattern, not decide it.

If the audit shows a small number of templates and no confusion, you probably do not need a counting system yet. If it shows repeated reuse and version drift, then measurement may be the right next step before any heavier automation.
